paper_id: Patil et al. - 2008 - SOLONet Sub-optimal location-aided overlay network for MANETs
title: SOLONet: Sub-optimal location-aided overlay network for MANETs
motivation: Overlay multicast gains are offset by overhead of precise location info distribution and maintenance in MANETs
problem_framing: Build efficient location-aided overlay trees without requiring expensive location broadcasts or per-node location tables
key_insight: Event-based cell-center updates achieve near-optimal trees without per-packet location headers or full topology knowledge
method_signature: Cell-partitioned topology with event-based location updates and local leader-based service discovery
evaluation_criteria: Performance vs optimal tree, scalability, reconnection costs under varying cell sizes and mobility
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: The resulting tree is sub-optimal; source assumes node location as cell center, not exact position
evidence_for_taste: performance gains are offset by overhead
doesn't require every packet to carry location info
strikes a good balance between advantages
places the minimum burden on each node
thinking_moves: Accepts sub-optimality as a design feature rather than a failure
Reframes accuracy vs cost tradeoff into a practical engineering problem
Verifies against idealized baseline to establish quality floor
Uses cell structure to localize computation and reduce broadcast scope
Discovers counter-intuitive result that smaller cells don't always increase reconnections
cites_own_work: Patil et al. 2004 (earlier SOLONet conference version)
